2608.03627.title: Unequal Verdicts: Investigating Gender Bias in LLM-Based Fake News Detection
2608.03627.paper_summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for automated fact-checking, yet their susceptibility to gender bias in this context remains underexplored. This study presents the first systematic investigation of gender bias in LLM-based fake news detection using real-world data. We augment the LIAR benchmark with three gender variants of speaker job titles (Neutral, Male, Female) for each statement to test whether veracity judgments vary solely based on gender presentation. Six state-of-the-art LLMs are evaluated across multiple bias and fairness metrics. All models exhibit gender sensitivity: 9.79%-35.13% of statements receive inconsistent labels across the three variants, with Male-Female comparisons showing 6.5%-23.6% flip rates. Two primary bias manifestations are identified: instability (inconsistent judgments) and directionality (systematic favoritism). Five models show statistically significant directional effects, with the strongest effects displaying male-skeptic patterns. These findings demonstrate that gender bias undermines both reliability and fairness in LLM-based fake news detection, highlighting the need for bias-aware evaluation and mitigation strategies. The augmented dataset is publicly released to support future research.
2608.03627.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在自動事實查核中的使用日益增多，但它們在這一背景下對性別偏見的敏感性仍然未被充分探討。這項研究首次系統性地調查了基於LLM的假新聞檢測中的性別偏見，使用了真實世界數據。我們在LIAR基準上增添了三種性別變體的發言者職稱（中性、男性、女性），以測試真實性判斷是否僅基於性別表現而有所不同。六個最先進的LLM在多個偏見和公平性指標上進行評估。所有模型都顯示出性別敏感性：9.79%-35.13%的陳述在三個變體中獲得不一致的標籤，男性與女性的比較顯示出6.5%-23.6%的翻轉率。識別出兩種主要的偏見表現：不穩定性（不一致的判斷）和方向性（系統性偏愛）。五個模型顯示出統計上顯著的方向性效應，最強的效應顯示出男性懷疑的模式。這些發現表明，性別偏見削弱了基於LLM的假新聞檢測的可靠性和公平性，突顯了對偏見意識評估和緩解策略的需求。增強的數據集已公開發布，以支持未來的研究。
